LaTeX source for a FAccT 2027 submission. Project argument and dates:

\subsubsection{Hard rule: Claude does not write paper prose}

FAccT prohibits the use of LLMs to generate text for publications, and
undisclosed or inaccurate content is grounds for desk rejection.
Therefore:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Never write or rewrite sentences in the paper} --- not drafts,
  not rephrasings, not ``light polish'', not typo fixes. This holds even
  when asked casually; if a request would put model-written words into
  the \texttt{.tex}, say so and offer critique instead.
\item
  \textbf{Claude may edit \texttt{.tex} markup only:} LaTeX commands and
  environments, \texttt{\textbackslash{}cite} keys,
  \texttt{\textbackslash{}input} structure, labels and refs,
  figure/table scaffolding, compile fixes.
\item
  \textbf{Prose feedback goes in chat} or a notes file
  (e.g.~\texttt{notes/review-*.md}) --- clearly marked as Claude's ---
  for the authors to act on in their own words.
\item
  \texttt{\%} comments in the \texttt{.tex} files are author-to-author
  notes. Don't delete or rewrite them.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{What Claude is for here}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Argument and structure critique: asserted-vs-demonstrated claims, gaps
  in the citation arc, places reviewers will push.
\item
  Checking that a cited source actually says what the text claims. Keep
  what a source argues separate from what the paper does with it.
\item
  Literature search --- every paper and claim verified by an author
  before it enters the bib.
\item
  LaTeX/acmart infrastructure, compile errors, page counts, anonymity
  audits, bib hygiene.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{GenAI disclosure log}

Every submission requires a Generative AI Usage Statement
(\texttt{sections/endmatter/genAI.tex}), and the author guide says to
err on the side of disclosure. Whenever Claude does something
disclosure-relevant --- literature search, idea generation, argument
critique, synthesizing notes, checking a technical claim --- append an
entry to \texttt{notes/genai-log.md} (date, model, task, what humans did
with the output). Pure LaTeX/compile help can be logged in aggregate.

\subsubsection{Submission checklist (anonymity and format)}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{\textbackslash{}documentclass{[}manuscript,screen,review,anonymous{]}\{acmart\}}
  (\texttt{anonymous} added 2026-10-26).
\item
  No author names, affiliations, ORCIDs, or identifying statements in
  the body; self-citations in third person.
\item
  No links to \texttt{github.com/{[}anonymized{]}/*} --- use an
  anonymized mirror if any code or data availability statement is added.
\item
  Endmatter at submission: \textbf{GenAI statement (required)}, ethical
  considerations (expected; must address close-reading a community-made
  jailbreak document, ENI; the subreddit reply corpus is not analyzed in
  this submission). Omit acknowledgements, author contributions,
  competing interests, and positionality if it identifies the authors.
  The endmatter files exist but are empty and not yet
  \texttt{\textbackslash{}input}.
\item
  Limitations belong in the main body, not the endmatter.
\item
  Length: ≤14 pages single-column including figures/tables; references
  unlimited; one extra page for endmatter only. Appendices allowed but
  reviewers needn't read them --- main text must stand alone.
\item
  References in ACM Reference Format if archival.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Register}

FAccT rewards showing the mechanism and naming the harm, staying in
conversation with theoretical frameworks (not just findings), and
uncomfortable claims whose discomfort is earned by evidence. It punishes
speculation dressed as analysis and technical fixes offered for
structural problems. Since the 2026-10-27 rescope the paper is a
framework-and-close-reading argument, not an empirical community study.
The citation registers are listed in \texttt{PROJECT.md} (technical
jailbreak literature as the foil, relational accounts of models, Stark
on coercive control as a regime). The Zachary / Pataranutaporn network
registers are no longer in this submission. Canonical background papers
are tagged \texttt{facct-background} (one entry
\texttt{facct\ background}) in the bib.

\subsubsection{Repo conventions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Sections: \texttt{sections/\textless{}name\textgreater{}.tex}
  (e.g.~\texttt{intro}, \texttt{relational}, \texttt{rlhf}),
  \texttt{\textbackslash{}input} from \texttt{main.tex} under a
  \texttt{\textbackslash{}section} heading there; endmatter in
  \texttt{sections/endmatter/}. The numbered \texttt{0N\_*} scheme was
  retired 2026-10-27.
\item
  Bibliography: \texttt{references.bib} is a Zotero export (keywords
  \texttt{author-a} / \texttt{author-b} mark who added an entry). Don't
  hand-edit it as if it were the source of truth --- report bib fixes so
  they can be made in Zotero.
\item
  Overleaf sync arrives as \texttt{overleaf-YYYY-MM-DD-*} branches
  merged by PR; pull before editing to avoid conflicts with Overleaf
  edits.
\item
  Notes in \texttt{notes/} are working documents.
  \texttt{notes/brainstorm-author-a.md} and
  \texttt{notes/brainstorm-author-b.md} are Claude-written (from
  dictation / Author B's research Claude), predate the rescope, and are
  not ground truth.
\item
  Commits by Claude: author
  \texttt{Claude\ \textless{}noreply@anthropic.com\textgreater{}}
  (Author A stays committer), small and legible. End every message with
  a
  \texttt{Co-Authored-By:\ Claude\ \textless{}model\ name\textgreater{}\ \textless{}noreply@anthropic.com\textgreater{}}
  trailer. The trailer is how the model is recorded.
\end{itemize}
